findings.claim: Diff redacts each input using only its own private fields. A private value identified in BEFORE can be printed unredacted from AFTER when its field is absent there, violating redaction everywhere across supplied evidence.
findings.verified_against:
Frozen CLI exit 0: BEFORE="USB:
  Device SECRET42:
    Serial Number: SECRET42
", AFTER="USB:
  Device SECRET42:
    Product ID: 0x201d
". stdout includes +  Device SECRET42:. Reverse direction has the analogous risk. No external disclosure performed.
findings.suggested_fix: Collect known private values from both inputs before rendering either side; apply their union to both inventories. Add CLI regression asserting SECRET42 absent in both directions while preserving device IDs.

findings.claim: Blanket substring replacement corrupts device identifiers when serial values overlap VID/PID text.
findings.verified_against:
Frozen usb-diff CLI with AFTER="USB:
  Vendor ID: 0x057e
  Product ID: 0x201d
  Serial Number: 0
" exits 0 and prints Vendor ID: [REDACTED]x[REDACTED]57e and Product ID: [REDACTED]x2[REDACTED]1d. Independently reproduced before parent reported same preliminary finding.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve typed vendor/product identifier fields while removing sensitive field values and repeated standalone private values. Add a short serial regression asserting exact VID/PID preservation.

findings.claim: A device heading containing Serial is mistaken for an empty sensitive property, so valid USB serial-adapter inventory fails closed rather than producing evidence.
findings.verified_against:
Frozen usb-diff with AFTER="USB:
  USB Serial:
    Vendor ID: 0x0403
    Product ID: 0x6001
    Serial Number: ABC123
" exits 1: USB inventory contains an empty or multiline private field. Parent reported preliminary finding; independently reproduced here. Snapshot uses same redactor.
findings.suggested_fix: Distinguish profiler device/container headings from sensitive property keys while retaining rejection of malformed sensitive properties. Add serial-adapter heading regression.
